content:
A married couple, married under the legal community property regime since 1994, are requesting the division of a real estate portfolio consisting of apartments, land and a villa under construction, after their separation in 2016 brought an end to the family property regime. The case falls under the dissolution of the community property regime (Art. 191 of the Italian Civil Code) and the consequent division of real estate under the ordinary community property regime. The main interpretative issue concerns the divisibility of an illegal property and the enforceability of private deeds signed by only one spouse with third-party creditors.
The Court applies the principle of the “legal possibility” of division, establishing that the non-compliance with urban planning regulations of the villa (Art. 46 of Presidential Decree 380/2001) precludes the dissolution of the judicial community, since the judge cannot endorse a transfer that would be prohibited by negotiation; the illegal property must therefore remain in undivided community. For the other assets, the judge deviates from the criterion of drawing lots (Art. 729 of the Italian Civil Code) in favour of direct allocation, motivated by reasons of subjective expediency and to avoid the functional depreciation of the shares. Finally, the right to reimbursement of 50% of the mortgage instalments paid exclusively by one spouse after the dissolution of the community property regime is recognised.
